data.title: InScope Art Festival Unveils Its New Beachfront Layout and Six Days of Programming Ahead of Its Miami Art Week Debut
data.description:
InScope Art Festival Unveils Its New Beachfront Layout and Six Days of Programming Ahead of Its Miami Art Week Debut

Glass-walled gallery pavilions, a monumental 45-foot architectural work of art, and an artist-created dive bar in place of the traditional VIP lounge anchor the 220,000-square-foot beachfront site. Programming runs from morning to night, featuring The Wellness Oasis® presented by Google Health with Oprah Winfrey, live musical performances, and evening events with Hypebeast, Modern Luxury, and Create & Cultivate. An interactive 3D model of the festival is now live at inscopeart.com.

InScope Art Festival today unveiled its complete beachfront layout and six-day program for its inaugural edition, taking place December 1–6, 2026, directly on the sands of South Beach at Ocean Drive and 8th Street during Miami Art Week.

This press release features multimedia. View the full release here: https://www.businesswire.com/news/home/20261127541212/en/

Spanning 220,000 square feet, InScope introduces a fundamentally different approach to the traditional art fair experience. In place of enclosed white pavilions, the festival features an indoor-outdoor environment built around contemporary art, architectural design, natural light, ocean views, and spaces that give people more reasons to come and stay.

Visitors can now explore the entire festival through an interactive 3D sitemap.

Rethinking the Art Fair Experience

The design began with a simple ambition: anyone familiar with this stretch of South Beach should cross the dunes and encounter something unlike anything they've experienced during Miami Art Week.

Rather than hiding its surroundings behind tent walls, InScope is designed to make the beachfront part of the experience. Intentional sight lines to the ocean, interconnected indoor and outdoor spaces, and unexpected artistic encounters create an environment where everyone enters through the same door, but no two visitors need to experience the festival in the same way.

Key elements of the design include:

The Glass Box: Visitors enter through a glass pavilion with an uninterrupted sight line through art, people, and monumental structures toward the Atlantic Ocean. Inside, guests will discover the Pixel Theory Lounge by New York artist Ceren Arslan, The Dive, and The Bistro.

Four Glass-Walled Gallery Pavilions: More than 70 galleries from 12 countries will present contemporary art across four monumental mono-slope pavilions, each spanning approximately 10,000 square feet. With rooflines ranging from 12 to 40 feet and glass walls that introduce natural light, the galleries offer a distinctive environment for discovering and collecting art.

A-Different Frame Presented by Aloyd: Created by Alain Perez, with design support from HOK + ROSSETTI, the centerpiece of the festival is a monumental 45-foot equilateral aluminum A-frame building constructed directly on the sand using Aloyd's proprietary architectural building system. The structure frames the ocean through its distinctive geometry and transforms throughout the week, serving as a lounge, listening room, wellness studio, and setting for evening dinners and receptions. The project marks the beginning of an annual architectural collaboration between InScope and Aloyd.

The Dive: In place of the traditional art fair VIP lounge, InScope introduces an artist-created dive bar featuring checkered floors, graffiti, a jukebox, and a pool table. Positioned at the festival's entrance and open to every attendee, The Dive sets the tone for a more welcoming and approachable art festival experience.

The Speakeasy: Designed by Chris Darsow and Michelle Marquez in collaboration with Art Force, The Speakeasy is an artist-created bar inspired by the intimacy of Japanese listening lounges. The freestanding 30-by-30-foot pavilion is wrapped in translucent crimson acrylic, glowing like a monumental lantern on the sand. Inside, a sculpted fabric canopy, low seating, warm lighting, and music create an intimate environment designed to encourage guests to slow down, listen, and connect.

The Bistro: Created by Chris Darsow and Michelle Marquez in collaboration with Art Force, The Bistro reimagines a French café in the heart of Cairo. A stone-inspired wall featuring a continuous-line mural, a working fountain, and warm teak latticework bring together European café culture, North African design, and contemporary art. The artist-designed space invites visitors to enjoy a coffee, engage in conversation, and take a moment between exploring the galleries.

The Commons: The outdoor heart of InScope connects The Glass Box, A-Different Frame, and the gallery pavilions through a collection of art installations, furnishings, shaded gathering areas, and walkways. The space encourages visitors to slow down, explore, and spend time together.

The Garden Salon: Created in collaboration with Mr. Flower Fantastic, The Garden Salon brings monumental floral sculptures into a 6,600-square-foot covered, open-air pavilion where art, nature, and conversation come together. The artist-designed space hosts artist conversations, educational sessions, live podcasts, and musical performances by day before transforming into a setting for private dinners, receptions, and parties in the evening.

The Oasis: Designed in collaboration with Chris Darsow, The Oasis is a 6,600-square-foot covered, open-air pavilion featuring a softly draped sage-green fabric ceiling, natural timber, and moss. The earthy palette and organic textures create a calming environment for wellness experiences, educational programming, and group activities by day, before transforming into a setting for private dinners and receptions in the evening.

Art extends well beyond the gallery walls. Every hospitality space, lounge, and activation across the site has been designed in collaboration with an artist as part of InScope's Feature Projects program, which brings together 21 projects featuring more than 50 artists.

The festival's physical environment is itself an artistic expression, one that will continue to evolve with each edition.

Programming That Gives People a Reason to Come and Stay

InScope's six-day program brings together influential voices across art, culture, wellness, wealth, entertainment, and the creator economy, with experiences designed to follow the rhythm of the day.

Mornings begin with group mental health & wellness experiences with The Wellness Oasis® and Human Proof inside A-Different Frame by Aloyd.

Afternoons feature artist conversations, educational sessions, and live podcasts on The Garden Salon Stage, beginning December 2. From Thursday through Sunday, Sunset Sessions will bring live music to the beachfront from 5 to 7 p.m., featuring Walshy Fire of Major Lazer, DJ Irie, Gia Fu, and a special surprise performance.

Evenings feature a series of private events hosted by leading media brands and cultural partners. Opening night on December 1 features the Hypebeast HypeAwards and Modern Luxury Miami Magazine's Art Edition celebration, followed by Art of the Party, hosted by Modern Luxury's Ocean Drive Magazine, on December 2. On December 3, Create & Cultivate brings its signature Supper Club to A-Different Frame, gathering 100 influential female founders and creators for an intimate evening. The event will feature a keynote by Krissy Cela and curated brand experiences from COVERGIRL and other leading partners. Additional private dinners and receptions throughout the week will connect leaders across wealth, art, culture, and entertainment.

On December 3 and 4, The Wellness Oasis® presented by Google Health will host two sold-out days of conversations, movement, workshops and breathwork, featuring Oprah Winfrey, Andre Agassi, Ken Griffey Jr., Naomi Osaka, Common, Napheesa Collier, Kevin Love, Dan Buettner, Gary Brecka, and dozens of other experts and advocates to help people with their mental health and overall well-being.

Building an Art Festival From the Ground Up

"The traditional art fair business model hasn't meaningfully changed in more than 50 years. For an industry built around creativity, I find that fascinating," said Matt Middleton, Co-Founder and CEO of InScope. "We started by asking ourselves what we would build if we weren't constrained by how art fairs have historically operated. Why would we hide one of the most desirable beachfront locations in Miami behind white tent walls? Why should someone interested in art have to leave the event to experience music, wellness, or interesting conversations?

"One of the most important metrics for us is how much time people choose to spend at InScope. The longer people stay, the more art they discover, the more artists and galleries they engage with, and the more opportunities they have to develop meaningful relationships. The event experience is our product, and we're building it from the ground up rather than following an established industry playbook."

"InScope was founded on a commitment to discovering, nurturing, and elevating artistic talent while creating new opportunities for people to engage with contemporary art," said Alexis Hubshman, Co-Founder and President of InScope. "I've seen firsthand how the most enduring relationships in art can begin with a single encounter, one that changes how someone experiences art and shapes their journey as a collector or patron. InScope is designed to create more opportunities for those encounters to happen and give them the time and space to develop into lifelong relationships."

Explore the Layout in 3D

An interactive 3D model of InScope's complete beachfront layout is now live at inscopeart.com, allowing visitors to explore the gallery pavilions, architectural installations, artist-designed hospitality spaces, and programming stages before arriving on-site.

Plan Your Visit

InScope Art Festival takes place December 2–6, 2026, directly on the sands of South Beach at Ocean Drive and 8th Street in Miami Beach, with a VIP and Media Preview on Tuesday, December 1.

Festival hours are 11 AM to 7 PM, with morning wellness programming beginning at 9:30 AM and private evening events continuing until 11 PM on select nights.

Tickets, the full programming schedule, and an interactive 3D model of the festival layout are available at inscopeart.com.

About InScope:

InScope is an art festival that brings together contemporary art, culture, and business directly on the beach during Miami Art Week. Built around emerging contemporary art and the people drawn to it, InScope combines gallery exhibitions, large-scale installations, cultural programming, hospitality, and experiences spanning wealth, technology, wellness, luxury, entertainment, music, and design.

By connecting artists, collectors, entrepreneurs, creators, investors, and cultural leaders, InScope creates opportunities for discovery, new ideas, and relationships that continue beyond the event. Learn more at inscopeart.com or follow InScope Art Festival on Instagram, X, and LinkedIn.

data.title: I'm in my 70s and buying a new BMW X1. Should I put my only son on the title?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

'Given my age, I never make a major new purchase without thinking about the future'

"At my age, safety and luxury are my two priorities." (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I'm in my 70s and, after 15 years driving my old car, it's finally time for me to buy a new one. It's a big deal for me and I'm aiming to spend $50,000 on a BMW X1. At my age, safety and luxury are my two priorities. I'm paying for it outright and I don't need a loan but, given my age, I never make a major new purchase without thinking about the future. I have one son and when I die, assuming the car still has value, I'd like him to inherit it.

Should I title the car in my name and leave it to him in my will, put us both on the title, or buy it in his name to save me all that hassle?

Safe Driver

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: 'I like the idea of a big return': My financial adviser wants me to invest $350,000 in a UAE data center. Is this risky?

You can leave your son the car through a transfer-on-death deed, although there are caveats.

Dear Driver,

It's not a good idea to add your son to the title.

Nor is it necessary to leave the car to your son in your will, or put his name on the title as sole owner. Probate is a public process and can take months, so the more assets that bypass probate, the better. That goes for your home, bank accounts, 401(k) and IRA. You can leave your son the car through a transfer-on-death deed, although there are caveats.

With a transfer-on-death deed, you have total control in the driver's seat and out of it. Assuming you predecease your son, all he has to do is bring your death certificate (sorry for being macabre), his I.D. and the title/transfer deed to the motor-vehicle agency in your state to complete the process. It could cost $15 to $75, assuming it's possible to do in your state.

Several states do not offer a standard transfer-on-death beneficiary designation for car titles. In those states, vehicle ownership must be transferred after the owner's death through probate, via inheritance, or through other procedures under their state's law. Bottom line: Not all states have a viable mechanism for transferring car ownership directly to a beneficiary.

Name a single primary and secondary beneficiary.

If your state doesn't offer transfer-on-death vehicle registration, you may still be able to bypass probate using joint title with rights of survivorship (not ideal, as it would give your son full ownership rights), a revocable living trust (assuming you also have other assets in the trust) and/or a small-estate affidavit.

In the event your state does permit transfer-on-death deeds for automobiles, keep in mind that it does not override a lien. "If there is an outstanding loan on the vehicle, the lienholder must be satisfied before the beneficiary can receive a clear title," according to SwiftProbate. "The beneficiary inherits both the vehicle and the responsibility to resolve the debt."

Name a single primary and secondary beneficiary. It can complicate things. "Some states allow you to name more than one transfer-on-death beneficiary," SwiftProbate says. "When the owner dies, all named beneficiaries must agree on what to do with the vehicle - keep it, sell it or transfer it to one of them. If they cannot agree, the situation can become contentious."

Related: 'My life could be cut short': I'm 55, married and have a brain tumor. Should I splash out on a $210,000 Porsche?

The perils of joint assets

But back to why you shouldn't put your son's name on the title of a car, house or any other asset. As Nathan B. Hannah, an attorney with the Arizona law firm DeConcini McDonald Yetwin & Lacy, points out, any financial problems your son has will become your financial problems if creditors go after your joint assets.

"For as long as I have been advising clients on estate planning and estate administration, I have seen elderly people who have made one or more of their children a joint owner on their house, their car, their bank account or all three," Hannah writes. "Another major risk of joint ownership is that the joint owner can appropriate the asset."

As for your new BMW X1: "If the title names parent or child as the owner, the child can pledge the title as security for a loan, or even transfer the title to a third party, without the parent's knowledge or consent," he notes. You may not think this is even a remotely likely scenario with your son, but no one who puts their child's name on an asset believes it would be possible.

Luxury and safety are two noble goals at any age.

Side note: Buying a $50,000 BMW X1 in your son's name constitutes a $50,000 gift that exceeds the annual gift-tax exclusion of $19,000, so you would be need to file a federal gift-tax return (Form 709) that applies the excess to your lifetime exemption. (The lifetime exemption is generous: $15 million for a single person and $30 million for a married couple.)

And, finally, insurers also require the policyholder (you, in this case) to own the car and price their coverage based on the primary driver's financial and driving record. Putting the car in your son's name while you drive it could lead to the insurance company denying a claim if you have an accident. That could end up costing you - and your son - thousands of dollars.

As for your choice of car? Luxury and safety are two noble goals at any age, but especially when you get older. Conservatively, try not to spend more than 5% of your net worth on an automobile - so if your net worth is $1 million or more, you can probably afford it, assuming that you have decent Social Security and retirement income from a 401(k) or IRA.

Drive safely, and enjoy your new set of wheels.

Related: My wife is bankrolling her family's trips to New York and it's draining our savings. Should I ask her to stop?

data.title: Eylsia Nicolas Passes One Billion Views in 2026 as "Santa Got Detained" Enters Groover Indie Top 10 and "Wake Me Up for Christmas" Preview Tops 5 Million Views
data.description:
JUPITER, FL / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / Singer-songwriter Eylsia Nicolas has passed one billion social media views in 2026. Her holiday single "Santa Got Detained," released November 19, is No. 4 on Groover's U.S. Indie chart and No. 8 on Groover's Global Indie chart. A Black Friday preview of "Wake Me Up for Christmas" has topped 5 million views across Instagram, Facebook and TikTok in the Philippines, ahead of the song's official release.

The momentum follows "Wake Me Up for Diwali Day," which drew more than 100 million views and launched Nicolas' Wake Me Up holiday series.

"Santa Got Detained" tells the story of Santa caught up in customs paperwork and fees on Christmas Eve. It mixes humor and social commentary, keeps a nonpartisan message and has a happy ending. "It's not a personal statement, it's a non-partisan idea of looking at a wider social perspective through humor," Nicolas said.

Music publications have praised the song's unusual approach:

  • Korliblog (Nov. 21) called it "a cheerful, story-driven Christmas song with a memorable premise and a generous spirit."
  • Lyrical Odyssey (Nov. 23) said the song "makes room not only for celebration but also for empathy and a little reflection," adding that Nicolas "brings humor and heart to those having a rough season, reminding us that compassion is also part of the holiday spirit."
  • New Fire Magazine (Nov. 24) wrote that Nicolas "walks the line between a cheeky premise and a sympathetic lens" and that the song "reminds us that Christmas celebrations belong to compassion, understanding, and hope."
  • Honk Magazine called it "a fun holiday release that offers a fresh outlook on the Christmas season by combining comedy, social commentary, and an encouraging message."
  • Kindline Magazine (Nov. 24) described the release as "blending holiday cheer, humour and social commentary."

Radio stations are adding the song too. Paris-based Volting Radio added "Santa Got Detained" to its rotation playlist. The station said the song "revisits the world of Christmas with an original approach, mixing humor with a look at certain social realities," and has "an identity all its own." Italy's SilverMusic Radio picked the track for its official Christmas programming, where it will air from December 1 through January 7, 2027.

Nicolas has more than one billion views in 2026 and more than 2.5 million followers across social platforms. With a Christmas song on international charts, she continues to build one of the most unconventional independent music brands working today.

Follow Eylsia Nicolas: https://eylsia.com/

Instagram: https://www.instagram.com/lisaeylsia

Facebook: https://facebook.com/eylsianicolas

YouTube: https://www.youtube.com/@eylsia

TikTok: https://tiktok.com/@lisaeylsia

******

About Eylsia Nicolas

Eylsia Nicolas (born Lisa Pamintuan) is an independent singer-songwriter based in Palm Beach, Florida, known for her Eylsia Orchestral Pop (EOP) sound. She passed 1 billion views across Facebook and Instagram in 2026 as an independent artist. She is a former Irish Open tennis champion, holds a Doctor of Jurisprudence and has served as president of the record label Deco Disc and of New York College of Health Professions. She founded the fashion line Nicolas of Palm Beach, owns the legacy brand Real Boxer and leads WorldIPI.com, an intellectual property research and development company. Her biography, "Hold On Another Day," is available at BookKards.com and on Amazon.

About Eylsia Nicolas LLC

Eylsia Nicolas LLC is an entertainment, media, and brand management company representing the career, creative works, products, and select commercial interests of Eylsia Nicolas. The company oversees activities spanning music, fashion, cosmetics, textiles, publishing, entertainment, personal appearances, speaking engagements, licensing, branded products, and related media ventures.

Jennifer Chen
Info@eylsia.com

data.title: Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico Announces the Results of the Initial Public Offering of FIBRA GAP, Totaling PS. 7,820.1 Million
data.description:
GUADALAJARA, Mexico, Nov. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE: PAC; BMV: GAP) (the “Company” or “GAP”) announces that the Initial Public Offering (“IPO”) of FIBRA GAP was successfully completed yesterday.

The offering was carried out under the ticker symbol “FGAP26” through the issuance of 391,004,247 Energy and Infrastructure Investment Trust Certificates (“CBFEs”) at a price of Ps. 20.00 per certificate, for a total amount of Ps. 7,820.1 million. The offering included participation from Pension Fund Administrators (“Afores”) and the general investing public.

The proceeds from the offering will be used to subscribe for shares representing the capital stock of the concession-holding companies for the twelve Mexican airports, as well as to cover issuance expenses. Once these expenses have been deducted, FIBRA GAP will make the corresponding capital contributions, acquiring a 3.98% equity stake in each of these companies. These funds will help finance the investments committed for 2027 under the 2025–2029 Master Development Program.

With this issuance, GAP diversifies its sources of financing and strengthens its capacity to continue executing its investment program, which is focused on the expansion and modernization of airport infrastructure in Mexico.

For all matters related to FIBRA GAP, please contact Gisela Murillo via email at gmurillo@aeropuertosgap.com.mx.

Company Description

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacífico, S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) operates 12 airports throughout Mexico’s Pacific region, including the major cities of Guadalajara and Tijuana, the four tourist destinations of Puerto Vallarta, Los Cabos, La Paz and Manzanillo, and six other mid-sized cities: Hermosillo, Guanajuato, Morelia, Aguascalientes, Mexicali, and Los Mochis. In February 2006, GAP’s shares were listed on the New York Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol “PAC” and on the Mexican Stock Exchange under the ticker symbol “GAP”. In April 2015, GAP acquired 100% of Desarrollo de Concessioner Aeroportuarias, S.L., which owns a majority stake in MBJ Airports Limited, a company operating Sangster International Airport in Montego Bay, Jamaica. In October 2018, GAP entered into a concession agreement for the Norman Manley International Airport operation in Kingston, Jamaica, and took control of the operation in October 2019.

data.title: UraniumX Announces Flow-Through Private Placement
data.description:
VANCOUVER, BC / ACCESS Newswire / November 27, 2026 / UraniumX Discovery Corp. (CSE:STMN)(OTCQB:STMXF)(FSE:Q7S) (the "Company" or "UraniumX") is pleased to announce a non-brokered private placement of up to 36,363,636 flow-through shares at a price of $0.055 per FT Share for aggregate gross proceeds of up to $2,000,000 (each a "FT Share") (the "Offering"). No warrants will be issued to subscribers in connection with the Offering. The Company may increase the size of the Offering to accommodate additional demand.

The FT Shares will qualify as "flow-through shares" within the meaning of subsection 66(15) of the Income Tax Act (Canada). The Company intends to use the gross proceeds from the sale of FT Shares to incur eligible" Canadian exploration expenses" that qualify as "flow-through critical mineral mining expenditures" within the meaning of subsection 127(9) of the Income Tax Act (Canada), which will be renounced to the subscribers in an amount not less than the subscription price of the FT Shares, with an effective date no later than December 31, 2026 and to incur such expenses on or before December 31, 2027.

Proceeds will fund the Company's ongoing exploration activities at Murphy Lake.

Closing of the Offering is subject to receipt of all necessary corporate and regulatory approvals, including the approval of the Canadian Securities Exchange. All securities issued under the Offering will be subject to a statutory hold period of four months and one day from the date of issuance.

The Company may pay finder's fees to eligible persons in connection with the Offering, in accordance with the policies of the Canadian Securities Exchange.

About UraniumX Discovery Corp.

UraniumX Discovery Corp. is a Canadian-based junior uranium exploration company focused on advancing uranium properties in Saskatchewan's Athabasca Basin, one of Canada's most active uranium districts. The Company's flagship Murphy Lake Uranium Property is located in the northeastern Athabasca Basin, where UraniumX is earning up to a 70% interest through an option agreement with F4 Uranium Corp. UraniumX additionally holds 100% interests in the Zoo Bay and NeoCore uranium properties, and is advancing a project generator approach across its broader portfolio by optioning non-core assets while retaining royalties and equity, allowing the Company to concentrate exploration capital on Murphy Lake.

data.title: I hate that Jensen Huang is back at Nvidia, but I love what it's done for my 401(k). Am I a hypocrite?
data.description:
By Quentin Fottrell

Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods

Jensen Huang, who on Monday returned as CEO of Nvidia. (Photo subject is a model.)

Dear Quentin,

I was paralyzed during the market downturn, so I have a question in the event that this bounce - led by the shocking and, in my opinion, unwelcome news that Jensen Huang has returned as Nvidia's (NVDA) CEO - does not last. No comment on that, as it happens, even though I have my opinions, like most people do.

I'm writing to you about my own strategy, not to pass judgment on other people's corporate decisions. During a market downturn, is it better for me to draw down cash from CDs for the next year or two rather than taking money from my equities and annuities at a loss? Where are the safe havens? I don't want to eat into my retirement savings.

Planning Ahead

You can email The Moneyist with any financial and ethical questions at qfottrell@marketwatch.com. The Moneyist regrets he cannot reply to questions individually.

Related: America is divided into two countries - Trump's pro-billionaires and Mamdani's anti-billionaires

Being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing.

Dear Planning,

It's fair to say that many people were surprised by Jensen Huang's return on Monday - and you are not alone in having strong opinions on that.

Some of the same people who cried foul over the fall in their 401(k)s and IRAs may well be rolling their eyes over the return of Huang to the helm of Nvidia, which now appears to be the cornerstone of the AI revolution, mostly due to its multibillion-dollar microchip business and proprietary software ecosystem. Indeed, the stock gave up some of Monday's gains on Tuesday as investors turned their attention to regulatory concerns about the export of U.S. microchips to China and elsewhere. Huang was effectively fired (he officially resigned) from the company a couple of weeks ago over his reported affairs with two employees, as well as one with a woman who has been accused of being a Chinese spy.

Commentators have questioned whether President Donald Trump overlooked the potential and alleged national-security threat by calling for Huang's return to Nvidia NVDA, thereby signaling that the company is too big to fail. Others bemoaned the decision by the company's board and wondered what the role of such boards is, if not to uphold professional, legal and personal standards. While low-wage American workers have been fired over bathroom breaks, skeptics may wonder if rules of conduct only apply to nonbillionaires.

It's OK to have joys and concerns about the billionaire class and your 401(k), even if the answers conflict with each other.

And, honestly, being paralyzed during the recent volatility in the market is not exactly a bad thing, either. Doing nothing and maintaining an even temperament is often the work of gods. Some people panic and sell, or move into real estate, bonds, or gold, and constantly check their 401(k) while getting upset over paper losses. Yet short-term swings won't have a big impact if they aren't about to retire or haven't just retired - especially if they have cash alternatives. How many times a day or week did you check your 401(k) when the market was on the rise? I'm guessing not a lot.

I sympathize with your urge to check. According to a 2026 report by the Investment Company Institute (ICI), a global trade association representing regulated funds and their shareholders, 81% of mutual fund-owning U.S. households hold stock funds - most of them inside workplace retirement plans. Because broad stock and index funds are heavily weighted toward mega-cap AI leaders like Nvidia, a significant share of American households are naturally exposed to those stocks. "Mutual funds play a key role in their households' balance sheets," the researchers wrote.

But back to the other questions in your letter: Yes, drawing from CDs and relying on annuity income can be a smart move. That assumes you don't have required minimum distributions from a traditional retirement account and your CDs have reached the end of their term. If you paid extra for a guaranteed lifetime income rider on your annuities - locking in an income stream if markets plummet or your account balance falls to zero - that will protect you during a correction, while fixed annuities aren't tied to the market's fortunes at all. Having cash alternatives helps you avoid "sequence-of-returns risk," where poor market performance in the early years of retirement puts pressure on a portfolio you're drawing from.

Don't miss: 'Nvidia's turmoil has me spooked': Is it time to sell my stocks and buy real estate?

Timing the market vs. managing risk

Darius Dale, founder and CEO of 42 Macro, a macroeconomic research and systematic risk-management firm, predicts that markets will return to a "risk-on market regime," where investors favor higher risk assets over safe havens, within a couple of months. "Hope is not an effective risk-management process," he says. "Positioning for the market regime helps investors avoid fear of missing out (FOMO) and fear of more losses (FOML). FOMO causes investors to buy cycle tops, and FOML causes investors to sell cycle lows. These are the two worst things any investor can do to their financial well-being."

As for your curiosity about safe havens, I can understand why you would consider them after such a volatile week, especially with lingering questions about the stock market's heavy dependence on AI. The right mix depends on your risk tolerance and, as Dale suggested, your expectations about the economic outlook, especially if you want to factor in how reliant the economy is becoming on AI. There are many paths to take. Andrew Clinton, CEO of Clinton Investment Management, suggests municipal bonds as a haven during a correction.

I can understand why you would look for safe havens, especially with lingering questions about the market's heavy dependence on AI.

Municipal bonds are, for the record, more appropriate for investors in higher tax brackets with money held in taxable accounts who live in high-tax states, and for retirees prioritizing cash flow and capital preservation. "Municipal bonds offer attractive tax-adjusted carry and stable underlying asset-class credit quality for investors seeking durable cash flows amidst equity-market volatility," he says. "Current municipal bond yields remain near the most attractive levels in decades."

Clinton also has a rosier outlook on the underlying strength of the U.S. economy than, perhaps, many folks. "Credit fundamentals remain strong, with default rates representing only a fraction of corporate default rates," he says. "Municipal issuers provide essential services such as airports, utilities and toll roads, generating durable cash flows with limited exposure to corporate earnings volatility. If inflation moderates and rates decline, municipals offer the potential for both attractive income and capital appreciation."

For other safe havens, consider shorter-duration bonds, mutual funds and exchange-traded funds that invest in bonds with maturities of less than five years, as well as Treasury inflation-protected securities (TIPS) backed by the U.S. Treasury to guard against rising prices. Give a thought to value-oriented and defensive sectors, including consumer-staples, utilities and healthcare stocks, for retired investors who seek stability over higher returns. Your lifestyle, the balances in your retirement accounts, your goals, your financial profile - whether you have a mortgage, debt or long-term-care insurance - and your views on AI all play a role.

Pausing during a storm does not mean you suffer from paralysis, and you don't have to like the news in order to plan around it.

Your letter attests to that.

Related: Is Social Security a Ponzi scheme? No. Don't get carried away with 1930s-era prophecies of doom.

Check out The Moneyist's private Facebook group, where members help answer life's thorniest money issues. Post your questions, weigh in on the latest Moneyist columns or email The Moneyist at qfottrell@marketwatch.com.

Rosen Law Firm Urges Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL, GOOG, GOOGM, GOOGN) Investors to Contact the Firm for Information About Their Rights

Rosen Law Firm, a global investor rights law firm, announces a class action lawsuit on behalf of purchasers of securities of Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL, GOOG, GOOGM, GOOGN) pursuant and/or traceable to the registration statement and related prospectuses (collectively, the “Offering Documents”) issued in connection with Alphabet's June 2026 underwritten offerings of Class A Common Stock, Class C Capital Stock, Series A Depositary Shares, and Series B Depositary Shares. Alphabet is a technology company.

For more information, submit a form, email attorney Phillip Kim, or give us a call at 866-767-3653.

The Allegations: Rosen Law Firm is Investigating the Allegations that Alphabet Inc. (NASDAQ: GOOGL, GOOG, GOOGM, GOOGN) Misled Investors Regarding its Business Operations.

According to the lawsuit, the Offering Documents contained false and misleading statements and omissions concerning Alphabet's financial results and trends. The Offering Documents represented that Alphabet's performance and outlook "could" be adversely impacted by innovations in its products and that operating results "could" be harmed by new investments in technologies. At the time the Offering Documents were issued, however, defendants' statements were materially false and the adverse conditions defendants warned "could" occur had already materialized. When the true details entered the market, the lawsuit claims that investors suffered damages.

What Now: You may be eligible to participate in the class action against Alphabet Inc. A lead plaintiff is a representative party who acts on behalf of other class members in directing the litigation. You do not have to participate in the case to be eligible for a recovery. If you choose to take no action, you can remain an absent class member. For more information, click here.

All representation is on a contingency fee basis. Shareholders pay no fees or expenses.

About Rosen Law Firm: Some law firms issuing releases about this matter do not actually litigate securities class actions. Rosen Law Firm does. Rosen Law Firm is a recognized leader in shareholder rights litigation, dedicated to helping shareholders recover losses, improving corporate governance structures, and holding company executives accountable for their wrongdoing. Since its inception, Rosen Law Firm has obtained over $2 billion for shareholders.
